facts.note: CORRECTED (fix wave, 2026-08-11). An earlier draft of this manifest wrongly reported this fact as a MAJOR FINDING contradicting cycle 1, by comparing the captured weights against a '20/20/20/16/16/10' pattern that exists nowhere in this project: the retired pre-2025 set was 20/20/20/16/16/8 (see wayback-lfca-2025-08), and the current set recorded in data/competencies.json since the 2025-09-16 revision is exactly the set this capture shows. `node -e "const c=require('./data/competencies.json');console.log(c.domains.map(d=>d.name+': '+d.weight+'%').join('\n'))"` confirms all six weights match this capture verbatim: Linux Fundamentals 16%, System Administration Fundamentals 30%, Cloud Computing Fundamentals 18%, Security Fundamentals 14%, DevOps Fundamentals 12%, IT Project Management Fundamentals 10%. The competency-list claims in the earlier draft were inverted the same way: data/competencies.json already records 'File Management Commands' and 'General Networking Commands' as removed in the 2025 update, Disaster Recovery as added, and Security Fundamentals as Security / Sensitive Data / Compliance -- every 'change' the earlier draft reported is this capture agreeing with cycle 1's recorded 2025 competency change set, not contradicting it. data/competencies.json is unchanged by this correction; it was correct all along.

facts.note: FINDING AND RESOLUTION. Cycle 1 (2026-08-09) and cycle 2 both explicitly checked this same page and found no question count anywhere in official sources; research/exam-mechanics.md recorded that absence at length and treated third-party 'commonly 60 questions' claims as unverified tier-3/4 noise. This 2026-08-11 capture reversed that finding: the page now states 60 questions (CNPA exam: 85), with the same 'generic rule + CNPA exception' structure this project already used to attribute the 90-minute duration and 75% passing score to LFCA via the certification page's own 'Multiple Choice Exam' classification. The number (60) matches the figure both prior cycles dismissed as unverified. This was escalated to the repository owner and ADOPTED on 2026-08-11 at HIGH confidence, inheriting the same classification-chain caveat research/exam-mechanics.md already attaches to the 75% pass mark (Section 4): it rests on the chain rather than an LFCA-specific statement naming '60' directly. See research/exam-mechanics.md Section 1 for the full reasoning and PROGRESS.md's 'Question count: adopted (2026-08-11)' subsection for the decision record.
